p01.best: Arrival given as 19:00; check-in closes 20:00; soak late, the baths run all night
p01.use: Cheap historic ryokan-hostel with natural hot-spring baths and a social lounge
p01.tip: BOOKED on Hostelworld for Nov 18: 7-bed tatami dorm, onsen included, balance paid at the desk. No car park: coin lot 35 m away

p02.best: Check in 15:00, outdoor bath at dusk, kaiseki dinner 18:00, second soak at 22:00
p02.use: Your luxury ryokan night: milky Owakudani sulphur water in Sengokuhara, kaiseki dinner, futon room
p02.tip: Swapped for K’s House Ito on Nov 18; nothing was booked here

p03.best: Weekday morning; sunset from the west cliffs
p03.use: Island temple-and-caves walk, sea air, Fuji on clear days; 1 hr from Shinjuku on the Odakyu line
p03.tip: Does not fit the 9 nights. Swap it in for Shimokitazawa on Nov 17 if you want sea over vintage

p04.best: Golden hour from Sumida Park on the Asakusa side for Skytree reflections
p04.use: Riverside walk linking Asakusa to Skytree
p04.tip: Walk Asakusa to Skytree along the river (25 min) instead of taking the train

p05.best: Late October for foliage; emerald water year-round
p05.use: Wild emerald river valley in the Kiso mountains
p05.tip: 4+ hrs each way from Tokyo and the foliage is mostly over by Nov 16. Save for a future car trip

p06.best: 09:00 opening on a weekday or 15:00 for last light; closed Mondays
p06.use: Calm green reset ten minutes from Kabukicho; maples turn from late November
p06.tip: ¥500, last entry 16:00, no alcohol inside. A good decompression stop after Nakano on Nov 17

p07.best: Late afternoon. Tokyo ginkgo is forecast to peak around Nov 26 this year, so Nov 24 should be near-golden
p07.use: The 300 m golden ginkgo tunnel of Jingu Gaien; festival stalls run mid Nov to early Dec (unconfirmed for 2026)
p07.tip: Five minutes from Aoyama-itchome station. An evening light-up from Nov 23 is rumoured; verify on the day

p08.best: At the 09:00 opening. Weekends and holidays in peak autumn have needed an online reservation (¥1,000) in recent years
p08.use: Small Zen temple with the most framed maple garden in Kyoto, a bamboo path and a hillside view
p08.tip: Pair with Ichijoji ramen street (10 min walk) and Shisen-do next door. Check enkouji.jp for the 2026 reservation window before Nov 21

p09.best: Nov 18 about 11:20, driven on the way to Fuji; the trees peak this week and the festival is the weekend you are in Kansai
p09.use: A 4 km ginkgo avenue with a street festival
p09.tip: Exit the Chuo at Hachioji IC, Route 20 west from Oiwake-cho to Takao station, back on at Takao-san IC; 15 min with the roof down

p10.best: 08:00 opening; the yukitsuri snow ropes go up from Nov 1; foliage mid to late Nov
p10.use: One of the three great gardens of Japan
p10.tip: Kanazawa is 2.5 hrs by Hokuriku Shinkansen; a two-day detour that does not fit. Next trip, with Toyama

p11.best: Arrive by 08:30, before the tour buses and before the deer are full
p11.use: Deer park, Todai-ji, mochi pounding at Nakatanidou
p11.tip: Kintetsu from Kyoto 35 min; continue to Osaka-Namba in 40 min

p12.best: 09:00 to 15:50, closed Mondays; free, no reservation needed
p12.use: Wide gravel grounds and the palace inside Kyoto Gyoen park; good ginkgo
p12.tip: Walkable from Tozando in 20 min. Skip it if Enkoji plus Gion already fill the day

p13.use: The most sacred Shinto shrine in Japan
p13.tip: Ise is 2 hrs from Osaka or Kyoto each way; it would cost you Nara and Osaka. Marked for a future trip

p14.best: Before 08:00 or after 16:30; mid-afternoon is a human traffic jam
p14.use: The bamboo grove, plus Tenryu-ji garden and Togetsukyo bridge
p14.tip: Arriving Nov 20 at noon, walk it around 15:30 in soft light and skip the centre if it is packed

p15.use: This bar is in Bengaluru, not Japan (saved by accident?)
p15.tip: Kept so your list stays complete

p16.best: Nikko foliage peaks early to mid November; mornings
p16.use: Vermilion bridge at the gateway to the Nikko shrines
p16.tip: 2 hrs from Asakusa by Tobu and a full day. Does not fit; Hakone takes the mountain slot

p17.use: City on the Sea of Japan coast, gateway to Tateyama
p17.tip: Out of range for this trip (4 hrs)

p18.best: After 16:00: smaller crowds, feeding time at the Pacific tank, open until 20:00
p18.use: One of the largest aquariums in the world; the whale shark tank is cinematic
p18.tip: Buy a timed e-ticket (about ¥2,700 to 3,000). Tempozan ferris wheel next door at sunset

p19.tip: Does not fit; the Fuji loop covers your mountain scenery need

p20.best: Shops open 12:00 to 20:00; Thursday to Sunday is liveliest
p20.use: Vintage clothing, record shops, punk bars; the locals version of Shimokitazawa
p20.tip: Look for Kita-Kore building, Sokkyou, the Pal arcade and the 7 pm izakaya crowd

p21.use: Showa-era temple town (Taishakuten, Tora-san) with dango stalls: old Tokyo at walking pace
p21.tip: 45 min from Ueno; the calmest option for your free day

p22.use: Nakano Broadway, Fujiya Camera and cheap izakaya all within 5 min of the station
p22.tip: Five minutes from Shinjuku on the Chuo line

p23.use: Stepping-stone pond garden in Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, the coffee district
p23.tip: Pair with Blue Bottle or Arise coffee; 15 min from Asakusa

p25.best: Fri and Sat until 20:00. Closed Mondays, but open on holiday Mondays like Nov 23 and closed the Tuesday after (verify)
p25.use: Samurai swords, armour, ukiyo-e; the katana rooms in the Honkan are the point for you
p25.tip: ¥1,000. Go on Nov 23 afternoon if the antique market ends early

p26.best: 10:00 to 17:00, closed Wednesdays; demonstrations through the day
p26.use: Antique music boxes and automata; quiet after the bamboo crowds

p27.use: Neon, host clubs, the Godzilla head, Kabukicho Tower arcades: your cyberpunk opener
p27.tip: Ignore touts and never follow anyone into a bar. Golden Gai and Omoide Yokocho are 5 min away

p28.best: Evening show, about 90 min; the November schedule is on gear.ac/en/ticket
p28.use: Non-verbal theatre of mime, breakdance, magic and projection mapping; world-class and language-free
p28.tip: Book online; premium seats about ¥6,000, cheaper at the back

p29.use: The graves of the 47 ronin; incense sold at the gate
p29.tip: Same site as Sengaku-ji on your shrine list; 10 min walk from Shinagawa

p30.best: 09:00 to 17:00; the hot-spring foot bath at 15:00 after the drive
p30.use: Sculpture park with the Picasso pavilion and a foot bath
p30.tip: Needed the Hakone afternoon that went to the Fuji west side; keep for a future Hakone day

p31.best: Plays every few minutes; best after dark
p31.use: The Cross Shinjuku Vision 3D cat at the east exit
p31.tip: Stand across the road from the station east exit

p32.use: The steaming hot-spring field in Kusatsu Onsen
p32.tip: 3.5 hrs from Tokyo; a different trip

p33.best: Dusk on Nov 18 is the famous frame, 10 min south of the Obuchi tea fields; only if the Ito buffer allows
p33.use: The bridge that looks like it climbs into Fuji; a 20 min car stop on the Fuji loop
p33.tip: Optional add after the tea fields; it costs 20 min of the drive to Ito

p34.best: Book the 15:45 slot: daylight, sunset at 16:28 and the night grid on one ticket
p34.use: The tallest view in Tokyo; the cyberpunk grid from 450 m
p34.tip: Tembo Deck about ¥2,100 online on weekdays; the 450 m combo about ¥3,100

p35.tip: ¥2,500 to 2,700; Ginza Mitsukoshi 9F; 15 min from the antique market

p36.tip: Amemura is the streetwear district; Triangle Park is the hangout

p37.best: 17:00 to 23:00, closed Sundays; book weeks ahead
p37.tip: Reserve through the restaurant or a concierge app (Omakase, Tableall). Ask for lighter, non-fishy neta

p38.use: Mentaiko baguette bakery, but in Fukuoka
p38.tip: Out of range; keep for a Kyushu trip

p39.best: Lunch only, 09:00 to 16:00; closed Tue, Sat and Sun
p39.use: Old-school yakiniku counter you marked as best yakiniku
p39.tip: Odd hours: it fits a Mon/Wed/Thu/Fri lunch, so Nov 23 (holiday, verify) or Nov 17

p41.best: Off-peak 15:00 to 17:00 to skip the queue
p41.use: Bullet-train conveyor sushi; order non-fish plates (tamago, inari, corn, chicken) with no judgement

p42.best: Lunch 11:30 to 14:00 or dinner 18:00 to 21:00; closed Mon and Tue
p42.tip: One of your four pizza picks; Seirinkan is the icon and closest to your route

p43.use: Neapolitan pizza near Togoshi Ginza (15 min walk)
p43.tip: Pair with the Togoshi Ginza street if you go

p44.best: Wed and Fri lunch, Sat and Sun afternoons only
p44.tip: Arrive at opening; it sells out

p45.use: Lunch-time pizza in Kagurazaka, a French-Japanese lane worth a wander

p46.use: The original Tokyo Neapolitan pizza (two pies only: margherita and marinara)
p46.tip: Two stops from Shibuya; the easiest pizza to fit, Nov 24 lunch

p47.best: 15:00 to 18:00 when the croquette stalls are busiest
p47.use: A 1.3 km shotengai: croquettes, oden, local life
p47.tip: Also on your shopping list; 20 min from Shibuya

p48.use: Tabelog number one kaiseki, ¥40,000+ a head
p48.tip: Near impossible to book from abroad; try a hotel concierge, otherwise keep it as a dream

p49.use: Pin and merch stop; American comfort food
p49.tip: Roppongi is also where teamLab Borderless lives (Azabudai Hills)

p50.best: 06:30 to 13:00, closed Wed and Sun, so Tuesday Nov 24 works
p50.use: The famous horumon-don and gyudon at Tsukiji outer market: your gyudon
p50.tip: Go at 07:00 with the market crowd; cash only; eat standing

p51.use: The hottest pizzeria in Tokyo right now
p51.tip: Expect a queue; one stop from Shibuya. Alternate to Seirinkan

p52.use: Wagyu burger and steak counter (your burger note)

p53.tip: Out of range; Tokyo ramen picks are in the suggestions

p54.best: 06:00 to 08:00 before the tour groups; the grounds stay open and lit until 23:00
p54.use: The oldest temple in Tokyo, Nakamise street, omikuji
p54.tip: Then Asakusa Underground Street and Kappabashi, 10 min walk

p55.best: Dusk; the lanterns are lit at night; open 24h
p55.use: The Gion shrine; walk Hanamikoji and Shirakawa after
p55.tip: Free. Saturday Nov 21 will be busy, so go after 17:00

p56.use: Tiny local shrine (3 reviews) in Tawaramoto town, Nara
p56.tip: A 40 min detour from Nara; only if it means something to you

p57.use: The Great Buddha hall; deer at the gate
p57.tip: ¥800; climb to the Nigatsu-do balcony for the view over Nara

p58.use: A small neighbourhood temple near Koenji (not the Kyoto moss temple)
p58.tip: If you meant Saiho-ji Kokedera in Kyoto, it needs a reservation months ahead. This one is a 10 min detour from Koenji

p59.use: Temple of the 47 ronin; the same site as the graveyard
p59.tip: Optional on Nov 24; 10 min from Shinagawa

p60.best: Sat and Sun 09:00 to 14:30; sellers pack up by noon
p60.use: The biggest flea market in Tokyo (300+ stalls)
p60.tip: Held Nov 21-22 while you are in Kansai. The Oedo Antique Market on Nov 23 is your replacement

p61.use: Huge used stock with a one-year warranty; use it to cross-check Fujiya prices
p61.tip: Used goods qualify for the tax refund; in-store prices match the website

p62.use: Vintage movie posters and old magazines; Jinbocho is 170 bookshops
p62.tip: Walk from Akihabara via Kanda Myojin and the Ochanomizu guitar street (25 min)

p63.use: Showa-era underground arcade with standing bars and cheap Thai and Vietnamese food
p63.tip: Under Asakusa station at the Ginza line exit

p64.best: 10:00 opening on a weekday; open until 20:30
p64.use: The best-value used Fujifilm bodies and lenses in Tokyo, honestly graded: buy the camera here
p64.tip: Used bodies are in the main shop, lenses in the annex. Ask for a body with the film simulations you want (X-T20 or X-E3 and up for Acros and Classic Chrome)

p65.use: Katana shop for real iaito (unsharpened practice swords), bokken, kendo gear and antique pieces
p65.tip: A bokken (¥3,000 to 8,000) flies in checked luggage. An iaito or replica (¥20,000 to 60,000) needs a shop certificate; Indian customs may treat blades as weapons, so a bokken is the safe buy

p66.best: 12:35 on Nov 18, straight off the Chuo Expressway after the ginkgo avenue
p66.use: The Honcho-dori photo: Showa shopfronts with Fuji filling the end of the street
p66.tip: Yoshida udon lunch nearby; 10 min from the Chureito pagoda

p67.use: Old-school Kita-ku shotengai, cheaper and less touristy than Togoshi
p67.tip: Near the Akabane standing bars; optional

p68.use: Collectibles, retro games, LSD Dream Emulator hunting
p68.tip: The Nakano Broadway complex is bigger; check both

p69.best: Shops 12:00 to 20:00; evenings for the live houses
p69.use: Vintage clothes, vinyl (Flash Disc Ranch, Jet Set), curry and small theatres

p70.use: Your chef knife and paring knife; English staff, free engraving
p70.tip: Gyuto 210 mm ¥15,000 to 30,000; pack in checked luggage. Kama-Asa and Tsubaya are two minutes away to compare

p71.best: Weekdays 10:00 to 17:00; many shops shut Sat and Sun
p71.use: Kitchen street: pots, ceramics, noren curtains, tea pots, plastic food
p71.tip: Nov 24 is a Tuesday, so it is open. Nov 23 (holiday) many shops close

p72.tip: Omiya is 40 min north of Tokyo; optional half-day only if the Nov 24 free day stays empty

p73.best: Most shops open from 12:00; mall 10:00 to 20:00
p73.use: Mandarake HQ (20+ shops), retro games, vintage watches, figures, Fujiya Camera next door
p73.tip: Mandarake Galaxy for retro consoles; LSD Dream Emulator is ¥30,000 to 60,000 when it appears

p74.use: Arcades (GiGO, Hey), Super Potato, Yodobashi, maid cafes, gachapon halls
p74.tip: GTA 6 ships Nov 19: ask the Yodobashi game floor about demo stations and check net cafes with PS5 rooms (Kaikatsu CLUB, select stores)

p75.best: 16:00 to 19:00 for the under-the-tracks izakaya scene
p75.use: Market street: snacks, Calbee, cheap sneakers, standing bars
p75.tip: Your salaryman night starts at a tachinomi under the Yamanote tracks

p76.use: HHKB and Realforce keyboards, Tamagotchi, Casio, Kit Kats, PS5 demo units
p76.tip: Tax refund desk per floor; from Nov 1 the refund is paid at the airport, so keep receipts

p77.use: The Lost in Translation bar on the 52nd floor; live jazz nightly
p77.tip: Arrive before 20:00 to skip the cover; cocktails ¥2,500+

p78.use: Chandelier-lit tiny bar in Omoide Yokocho; ¥500 seat charge
p78.tip: Omoide Yokocho is yakitori alleys; start here, end in Golden Gai

p79.best: 09:00 to 18:00, closed Tuesdays; mornings for fresh dango
p79.use: Mitarashi dango from the 85-year-old wagashi master in the video
p79.tip: 50 min from Akihabara on the JR Musashino line; only if the Nov 24 free day has a spare half day

p80.best: Weekday morning; 1 h 45 from Shinjuku (Chuo line → Ome line to Hatonosu)
p80.use: Gateway to the Hatonosu Gorge walk: emerald river, suspension bridge, a cliff-side cafe; the closest deep-nature fix to Tokyo
p80.tip: Free-day option for Nov 24: 3–4 h round trip. Last foliage of the trip around Nov 20–25

p81.best: Nov 18 about 14:45, between Chureito and Lake Motosu on Route 139
p81.use: The smallest and quietest of the Five Lakes; Fuji reflected with no crowds. Your list
p81.tip: 10 min detour from Asagiri Kogen; small free lot at the north shore

p82.best: Late morning; 2 h 15 by car from Kyoto, 1 h 30 from Nara
p82.use: Mitarai Valley: emerald pools, waterfalls and suspension bridges along a 3 km gorge path. Your “beautiful water” note. Foliage peaks early–mid Nov, still good late Nov
p82.tip: Car only. Parking ¥500 at the Mitarai entrance; walk the gorge path to Tenkawa (2 h) or out-and-back 90 min. Pair with Nara on the way back

p83.use: Katsunuma: the wine valley north of Fuji (your “grape place?”). Grape harvest is over by November, but 30 wineries pour tastings and the Budo-no-oka hill has the view
p83.tip: Alternate end to the Fuji loop: Kawaguchiko → Misaka Pass → Katsunuma → Chuo Expressway to Tokyo; replaces Asagiri and the Fuji city bridge

p84.use: teamLab Planets: walk-through water and mirror rooms; the famous one. 30 min from CITAN by the Hibiya line and Yurikamome, 10 min from Omoren Ariake
p84.tip: Wednesday Nov 18 08:00 ticket, 90 min, then pick up the Roadster at 10:00. Book on teamlab.art

p85.use: Bunkoya-Oozeki: embroidered leather wallets and kawaii coin purses (your list)
p85.tip: Two minutes from Senso-ji; fits the Nov 24 Asakusa morning

p86.use: New York Joe: thrift priced by weight, in a converted bathhouse (your list)
p86.tip: Add to the Shimokitazawa stop on Nov 17

p87.use: Radio Center: the original 1950s electronics arcade under the tracks; parts, tubes, oddities (your list)
p87.tip: Next to Akihabara station; fits the Nov 23 afternoon
